chat: Which is faster, a jet or a biplane?
options: A jet is much more faster than a biplane.
A jet is much faster than a biplane.
A jet is much fastest than a biplane.
questions.rule: Short adjectives add -er before than; never use more with -er.

options: Arjan Singh is honoured by the government.

options: Our captain not only bats well but also bowls fast.
Our captain not only bats well but also bowl fast.
Our captain not only bats well but bowls also fast.

options: Having complete his course, he joined the squadron.

Having completed his course, he join the squadron.

options: Having ran ten rounds, I need some rest.

options: No other air chief of India was so greater as Arjan Singh.
No other air chief of India was as great than Arjan Singh.
No other air chief of India was as great as Arjan Singh.

options: Not only he flew fighters, but he also flew transport aircraft.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with 'not only ... but also'.
questions.rule: Put not only and but also before matching parts: a pilot / an ambassador.

options: Yes, I not only cleaned it but also arranged my books.
Yes, I not only cleaned it but also arrange my books.
Yes, I not only clean it but also arranged my books.
questions.rule: Both verbs after not only / but also must be in the same tense: cleaned, arranged.

options: Yes, it was announced an hour ago.
Yes, it was announce an hour ago.
Yes, it is announced an hour ago.
questions.rule: ago needs the simple past; passive: was announced.

questions.source: The squadron was led by Arjan Singh.
options: Arjan Singh was leading by the squadron.
questions.rule: Keep the tense: was led becomes led, and the doer becomes the subject.

questions.source: He was a fearless pilot and also a great leader.
options: Not only was he a fearless pilot but also a great leader.
Not only he was a fearless pilot but also a great leader.
Not only was he a fearless pilot but a great leader also was.
questions.rule: Not only at the start takes question order: was he ... but also ...

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this paragraph.

options: The new runway is being build near our town.

options: Each of the pilots has been given a medal.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with a superlative.
questions.rule: Superlative: the + -est form, followed by in + a group or place.

chat: Did you finish the fact file?
options: Yes. Having reading the article twice, I found all the dates.
Yes. Having read the article twice, I found all the dates.
Yes. Having read the article twice, I find all the dates.
questions.rule: Having + past participle (read), and the main verb stays in the past: found.

questions.source: Arjan Singh led the squadron bravely. He was awarded the DFC.
options: Having lead the squadron bravely, Arjan Singh was awarded the DFC.
Having led the squadron bravely, Arjan Singh awarded the DFC.
Having led the squadron bravely, Arjan Singh was awarded the DFC.
questions.rule: Having + past participle (led) for the first action; keep the passive: was awarded.

questions.source: Very few air forces are as large as the IAF.
options: The IAF is larger than most other air force.
The IAF is more larger than most other air forces.
The IAF is larger than most other air forces.

options: Seldom India has seen such a brave air chief.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

questions.after: he fly over sixty types of aircraft, but he also kept his flying skills till the end.
questions.rule: Past story + base verb fly: Not only did he fly.
Passive question: By whom + was + subject + past participle?

chat: Is Mount Everest higher than K2?
options: Yes, it is higher than any mountain in the world.
Yes, it is higher than any other mountain in the world.
Yes, it is highest than any other mountain in the world.
questions.rule: Everest is itself a mountain, so say higher than any other mountain.

options: It was stopped because of the heavy rein.
It was stopped because of the heavy rain.
It was stop because of the heavy rain.

Was he award the DFC by the Supreme Allied Commander?
